description: MLIR (Multi-Level Intermediate Representation) decomposed. LLVM project's IR-of-IRs framework. Dialects, operations, types, attributes. Progressive lowering. Pass infrastructure. Used by TensorFlow XLA, PyTorch 2.0's Inductor, IREE, CIRCT (hardware), Mojo, Flang.

sub_mechanisms.name: MLIR_operation
sub_mechanisms.definition: Fundamental unit in MLIR. Has a name (dialect-qualified, e.g., 'arith.addi'), operands, results, attributes, regions.
sub_mechanisms.why: Universal representation. Same data model handles abstract (matmul) + concrete (i32 add). Operation classes hierarchy enables generic transformations across dialects.

sub_mechanisms.name: MLIR_dialect
sub_mechanisms.definition: Namespaced set of operations, types, attributes. arith (arithmetic), affine (affine loops), scf (structured control flow), linalg (linear algebra), gpu, llvm.
sub_mechanisms.why: Modular extension mechanism. Each dialect captures domain-specific structure. Lowering progressively rewrites from high-level dialects to low-level. Avoids the 'one true IR' constraint.

sub_mechanisms.name: MLIR_type_system
sub_mechanisms.definition: Dialect-extensible type hierarchy. Built-in types (i32, f64, vector, tensor) + custom dialect types (linalg structures, gpu memref).
sub_mechanisms.why: Type system carries domain semantics. Tensor types track shape + element type + encoding. Lets type-driven dispatch in passes ('apply this transformation to tensor ops only').

sub_mechanisms.name: MLIR_attribute
sub_mechanisms.definition: Compile-time constant attached to operations. Integer values, strings, arrays, dialect-specific attributes (affine maps, gpu launch configurations).
sub_mechanisms.why: Encodes operation parameters that aren't runtime values: loop trip counts, tile sizes, kernel launch dimensions. Pass infrastructure can match + rewrite based on attribute values.

sub_mechanisms.name: MLIR_region_block
sub_mechanisms.definition: Operations can contain regions (nested IR), regions contain basic blocks (sequences of operations). Function bodies are regions; loops are operations with body regions.
sub_mechanisms.why: Hierarchical IR. Structured control flow (loops, conditionals) is nested operations + regions. Avoids the unstructured CFG of LLVM IR. Enables structural pattern matching on loops.

sub_mechanisms.name: progressive_lowering
sub_mechanisms.definition: Compilation pipeline applies lowering passes, each transforming one dialect's operations into operations of a lower-level dialect.
sub_mechanisms.why: From high-level (linalg.matmul) progressively to lower (affine.for nests, then scf.for, then llvm dialect, then LLVM IR). Each step reveals more detail. Optimisations apply at each level.

sub_mechanisms.name: linalg_dialect
sub_mechanisms.definition: Linear algebra dialect: matmul, conv, reduce as structured operations on tensors. Compiler-friendly abstractions for ML workloads.
sub_mechanisms.why: ML compilation entry point. Operations carry algebraic semantics (matmul's commutativity properties). Tiling, fusion, vectorisation apply at this level before lowering.

sub_mechanisms.name: affine_dialect
sub_mechanisms.definition: Affine loop dialect: affine.for nests with affine bounds + memory access patterns. Polyhedral analysis applies here.
sub_mechanisms.why: Constrained form enabling provably-optimal transformations. Polyhedral tiling, parallelisation, vectorisation work on affine code. Bridges high-level + low-level via well-understood theory.

sub_mechanisms.name: scf_dialect
sub_mechanisms.definition: Structured Control Flow dialect: scf.for, scf.if, scf.while. More general than affine; less structured than llvm CFG.
sub_mechanisms.why: Captures structured control without affine constraints. Intermediate between high-level (parallel for) and low-level (basic blocks + jumps). Many transformations preserve structure at this level.

sub_mechanisms.name: MLIR_pass_infrastructure
sub_mechanisms.definition: Pass manager + pass abstraction. Passes apply to specific dialects or specific operation types. Pipelines compose passes.
sub_mechanisms.why: Compiler engineer assembles pipelines from passes. Generic infrastructure (pass scheduling, parallel execution, debug instrumentation) shared across dialects. Same shape as LLVM's pass manager but extended.

sub_mechanisms.name: MLIR_dialect_conversion
sub_mechanisms.definition: Framework for systematic lowering between dialects. Pattern rewrites + type conversion + legalisation.
sub_mechanisms.why: Lowering pipelines need consistent infrastructure. Dialect conversion handles type substitution + operation replacement uniformly. Reduces lowering complexity from O(N²) ad-hoc rewrites to declarative patterns.

sub_mechanisms.name: TensorFlow_XLA_uses_MLIR
sub_mechanisms.definition: TensorFlow's XLA compiler migrated to MLIR-based representation. HLO operations as MLIR dialect.
sub_mechanisms.why: First major MLIR user. Demonstrated MLIR's value at production scale. PyTorch 2.0's Inductor + IREE follow similar pattern. Established MLIR as the modern ML compiler infrastructure.

derivation_rules.name: dialect_separation_enables_modular_optimisation
if: a compiler has dialects at different abstraction levels
then: optimisations apply at the appropriate level
derivation_rules.why: Matmul transformations (tiling, fusion) apply on linalg dialect. Loop transformations (vectorisation, parallelisation) apply on affine. Low-level instruction selection on llvm dialect. Each level has its own optimisation opportunities.

derivation_rules.name: progressive_lowering_preserves_high_level_semantics
if: high-level operations are lowered through intermediate dialects
then: high-level semantic information guides each level's optimisations
derivation_rules.why: Lower-level IR (LLVM IR) loses information from higher (matmul → many adds + muls). Progressive lowering carries information forward as long as useful. Matmul's structure enables tiling decisions impossible at LLVM IR level.

derivation_rules.name: shared_infrastructure_amortises_compiler_construction
then: each saves on pass manager, debug, IR validation costs
derivation_rules.why: Building a compiler from scratch is enormous work. Sharing MLIR's framework lets ML compilers (XLA, Inductor, IREE), hardware compilers (CIRCT), language frontends (Flang, Mojo) reuse infrastructure. Reduces marginal cost of new compiler.

derivation_rules.name: structured_regions_preserve_loop_structure
if: IR represents loops as operations with body regions
then: loop transformations work directly on the structured form
derivation_rules.why: LLVM IR's basic-block-and-branch loops require loop analysis to recognise. Structured loops (scf.for, affine.for) are explicit; transformations apply directly. Loses some flexibility (unstructured control flow); gains transformation simplicity.

derivation_rules.name: type_system_extension_carries_domain_information
derivation_rules.why: Tensor types carrying shape + element type let pass match 'apply to ranked tensors'. Memref types carry layout + memory space. Type extension is how MLIR adapts to wildly different domains (ML, hardware, languages) without losing generality.
